_comment: Copy to ~/.claude/protected-zones.json and edit. This file is READ BY the
PreToolUse hook scripts/protected-path-denylist.ps1, which turns each entry into a
hard write-gate: Edit/Write/NotebookEdit/MultiEdit on a path inside the zone, and
Bash commands that pair a zone path with a mutation token (rm, mv, >, sed -i, ...),
are DENIED. Reads always pass - a protected zone is read-only, not no-access.
match  : a lowercase, forward-slash path fragment, matched literally against the
normalized path. A boundary (end / slash / space / quote) is appended, so
A fragment that is a prefix of another zone catches both.
why    : shown to the agent when it is blocked. Say why, so it stops arguing.
unlock : OPTIONAL. Path, relative to your home dir, of a file you create to grant
a supervised 24h write window (put an ISO-8601 timestamp inside it).
Omit the field entirely for a zone that must never be writable.
No config file => no zones => the hook exits 0 and the prose rule in CLAUDE.md is
your only guard. Keep this file out of git (it names your real folders):

zones.why: <project> (protected zone, writes need an explicit supervised GO)
